clue.text: Out of sight, out of mind

definitions.meaning: hidden from view, as something gone past a curve in the road is

explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the proverb 'out of sight, out of mind', but the two halves are separate definitions of one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, a thing past a curve is out of view; idiomatically, someone gone that way is mad.

clue.text: Sir upset with a form of bile -that's laughable

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word Sir upside down, so it reads from the bottom
a form of says the letters of bile are put into a different shape

explanation.surface: A knight gets queasy over his bile, which is a comic sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SIR into RIS; 'a form of' rearranges BILE into IBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something risible provokes mocking laughter, so it is ridiculous.

clue.text: I turned round to find it had not been tested

indicators.note: round says the letters of I and turned are spun about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone spins about and discovers a thing nobody had tried out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges I plus TURNED; 'turned' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Untested and untried are synonyms: neither has yet been put to proof.

clue.text: Mystery runner in a nightmare

definitions.meaning: a racehorse or candidate whose ability is unknown
read whimsically as a mare of the night, a black steed

explanation.walkthrough: 'nightmare' is split into night + mare, a horse in the dark; 'in a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An unknown contender is a proverbial unknown-quantity horse; a night mare would be a black one.

clue.text: Mob the store, from the sound of it

indicators.note: says the word for the store is said out loud, giving a word with a different spelling

parts.note: a hoard is a stockpile or stash

explanation.surface: A crowd descends on the shop, judging by the racket.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a large unruly crowd, a throng.

clue.text: Spanned new grid included in plot

indicators.note: included in puts the reworked letters inside the word for the plot

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot

indicators.note: new says the letters of grid are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone crossed over after a fresh grid went into the scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns GRID into RIDG, and 'included in' sets it inside BED.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridge a gap is to cross or span it.

clue.text: Little room in no Scottish aircraft enclosure

indicators.note: in puts the word for the little room inside the Scots word for no

parts.note: nae is the Scots form of no
a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery

explanation.surface: A tiny chamber with no Scottish connection inside a plane's housing.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacelle is the streamlined housing for an aircraft engine or crew.

clue.text: Strike call at the end of the innings

definitions.meaning: the shout of a union official calling workers out

definitions.text: at the end of the innings
definitions.meaning: when a cricket side's batting is over, all its players are out

explanation.walkthrough: An innings is a cricket team's turn at batting.
explanation.definitionFit: A union leader cries it to start a walkout; at the close of a cricket innings every batter is dismissed.

clue.text: Guest finds it hidden in the mask

indicators.note: hidden in says the word it is placed within the mask word

parts.note: a visor is a face-covering, part of a helmet

explanation.surface: A guest arrives concealing something behind a mask.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor is someone calling on you, a caller.

clue.text: Right racial disturbance on a train

indicators.note: disturbance says the letters of racial are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A racially motivated fracas breaks out on a train.
explanation.definitionFit: A railcar is a self-propelled rail coach, a small one-carriage locomotive service.

clue.text: Getting one's own back

parts.note: reads like taking revenge, but means literally reclaiming property one owns, as a lender does with goods

explanation.surface: Taking revenge on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A creditor reclaiming goods for unpaid debt takes back ownership.

clue.text: Nonsense, it can be thrown away as worthless

definitions.text: it can be thrown away as worthless

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both drivel in speech and garbage that is discarded.

clue.text: Encourage turn over of drink

parts.note: to egg on is to urge or encourage
to flip is to turn over

explanation.surface: Urging someone to hand over a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg flip is a drink of beaten egg with milk or spirits, like eggnog.

clue.text: Generate again in the rose garden?

indicators.note: in puts the word for again inside the garden word

parts.note: a rose bed is a garden plot of roses
re- is the prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: Propagating fresh roses once more in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To breed is to produce offspring, to beget.

clue.text: Prepare to give another send-off

parts.note: posting a letter on again means writing a fresh destination on it, a second dispatch rather than a farewell party

explanation.surface: Getting ready to throw a second farewell do.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-marking an envelope with a new destination sends it off once more.

clue.text: Paint does deteriorate in Australasia

indicators.note: deteriorate says the letters of paint does fall apart and are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Paintwork perishes in the Australian climate.
explanation.definitionFit: The antipodes is the British name for Australia and New Zealand, the far side of the globe.

clue.text: Put off a man from using a cleansing agent

parts.note: to deter is to put off or discourage
a gent is a gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: Discouraging a fellow from using soap.
explanation.definitionFit: A detergent is a soap-like cleaner for washing.

clue.text: Girl moves her seat

indicators.note: moves says the letters of her seat shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A young woman changes where she sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Theresa is a female first name.

clue.text: Withdraw offer of some more tractors

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A farmer withdraws an offer of extra tractors.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract an offer is to take it back.

clue.text: Class of actors get the point

parts.note: the cast is the company of actors in a play
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Performers grasp what the lesson is about.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class, especially in India.

clue.text: Bouquet to wilt in the middle

indicators.note: in puts the word for wilt within the word for the middle

parts.note: the core is the centre of something
to sag is to droop or wilt

explanation.surface: Flowers start to droop at the centre of the arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsage is a small spray of flowers worn on a dress.

clue.text: Esparto cultivated on the coast

indicators.note: cultivated says the letters of Esparto are worked like soil into a new form

explanation.surface: Esparto grass is grown by the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivated' rearranges ESPARTO. Esparto is a grass used for paper and rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaport is a harbour town lying beside the sea.

clue.text: Surpass with open work

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Outdoing others with openwork craft.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtop is to rise above or exceed.

clue.text: Penny moved only one power supporter

indicators.note: moved says the letters of only are shifted around

explanation.surface: A girl named Penny relocates a lone backer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pylon is a tower carrying electric power lines.

clue.text: Maybe exercises Dicky Sharp

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercises

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for faulty or shaky, so the letters of Sharp are jumbled

explanation.surface: A fellow called Dicky Sharp might be working out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' rearranges SHARP into RHAPS; it looks like a first name but is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Perhaps and maybe both express possibility.

clue.text: All the people, it might be said, on the road to the Palace

definitions.meaning: everyone, read as a two-word phrase '...'
the London avenue leading to Buckingham Palace

explanation.walkthrough: 'it might be said' hints that the two readings sound alike: the same letters split differently. The Mall is the grand road in London ending at Buckingham Palace.
explanation.definitionFit: Respaced, the letters say everybody; as written, they name London's ceremonial avenue to Buckingham Palace.

clue.text: Monster accepts nothing for the cavalryman

indicators.note: accepts means the monster word takes in the letter for nothing

parts.note: a dragon is a mythical monster
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A monster accepts nothing on behalf of the cavalryman.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoon was a mounted infantry soldier.

clue.text: In decline despite having broken a personal record

definitions.text: In decline despite having broken a personal record

parts.words: In decline despite having broken a personal record
parts.note: an athlete who beat a personal best has literally gone beyond it, yet the phrase means no longer at one's peak

explanation.surface: An ageing athlete sets a personal record yet is fading.
explanation.definitionFit: Being over the hill means one's peak years are behind one.
